design.purpose: every Phase-4 claim that was INFERRED rather than measured, tested with a stated falsifier

T8_aggregator_ratio.claim: the per-stock ratio of the mean-based to the median-based unconditional sd is 1.354 [IQR 1.286, 1.452] (P4-1), which is the whole of Phase 3's apparent level gap
T8_aggregator_ratio.note: s_A is the anchor the variance identity targets; the phase multipliers' reference is the per-stock MEDIAN of rolling-21d RV. The two differ by this ratio, which is why median-referenced multipliers applied to a mean-anchored base looked like a level defect

T1_convexity_endpoint.claim: the panel's run-ups decelerate (P4-8), so a super-exponential mania is contradicted
T1_convexity_endpoint.falsifier: if the deceleration disappears once the endpoint constraint is removed, the measurement is an artefact of defining a run-up by a local maximum at its top

b_minus21.description: [start, top-21] -- past the +/-10 d local-max constraint

c_fixed_horizon.description: [start, start+504] -- the END is not selected on price at all

T1_convexity_endpoint.verdict: REAL -- the deceleration survives removing the endpoint constraint, so P4-8 stands

T4_ks_floor.claim: about 2,000 seeds would bring the KS null floor to 0.10 (P4-9)
T4_ks_floor.falsifier: measure the floor at each n and read off the n that reaches 0.10
T4_ks_floor.verdict: the bound becomes attainable at about 4000 seeds

T5_residual.claim: the deployed excess over s_A is the benchmark's own scenario mix (P4-1)
T5_residual.falsifier: if one phase's contribution accounts for the residual, it is that phase's level and not the mix
T5_residual.note: panel weights come from E3.3's FIXED windows, so they measure the share of panel days those windows cover rather than a phase-dating of the whole panel; the decomposition shows where the variance sits, and is not a re-weighting that could be adopted

T3_item10_cause.claim: checklist item 10 is inert BECAUSE E4.2 draws delta from the panel's depth distribution, so the crash_discount arm factor no longer changes anything
T3_item10_cause.falsifier: if the partial R^2 of crash_discount is also near zero under the v2 schedule, the cause is something else
T3_item10_cause.verdict: CONFIRMED -- crash_discount drives MDD under v2 and does not under v21

T6_control_would_pass.claim: adopting A, B or D closes weakness items 18 and 42 (P4-9)
T6_control_would_pass.falsifier: measure the accepted-vs-rejected x distribution under each definition; if A/B/D still select on x the claim fails
T6_control_would_pass.threshold_note: the comparison is against a null computed at each definition's OWN achieved n_accepted / n_rejected, not against a fixed distance; a fixed 0.20 would have called every definition a selector, which is why the first version of this test did
T6_control_would_pass.verdict: NOT ESTABLISHED AT THIS n, DIRECTION CLEAR. Every definition's KS exceeds its own null p95, but by amounts that differ by a factor of about 18: A/B/D by 0.0042 and C by 0.0762. At n_rejected = 44 (A/B/D) the test has very little power in either direction -- T4 measured that this family of KS comparisons needs roughly 4,000 seeds to be decidable at D0 = 0.10. So the claim 'adopting A, B or D closes items 18 and 42' is NEITHER confirmed NOR refuted here; what IS measured is that C's selection is an order of magnitude larger than A/B/D's, and that A/B/D carry no x-band at all so any residual is rejection on V growth, which the engine makes independent of x.

T7_multi_asset.claim: v2's multi-asset extension puts every asset in the same event on the same days, i.e. a common-factor loading of 1.0 (P4-16)
T7_multi_asset.falsifier: generate 3-asset paths and measure the realised cross-sectional drawdown share
T7_multi_asset.verdict: CONFIRMED AS A DIRECTION but not as the number 1.0: the realised loading is 0.364 against the panel's 0.236; P4-16's wording must be corrected to the measured value
